title: AWL Sublist 9
description: Las 60 palabras de la sublista 9 de la Academic Word List, con definición, traducción, ejemplo académico, colocaciones y familia léxica.

cards.definition: To provide space or housing for people; to consider or adapt to different needs.
cards.es: alojar, dar cabida a; adaptarse a
cards.example: The new stadium can accommodate up to 60,000 spectators.
cards.warning: Ortografía: doble c y doble m. "Accommodation" (alojamiento) es incontable en inglés británico.

cards.definition: A comparison between two things that shows how they are similar.
cards.example: The author draws an analogy between the human brain and a computer.

cards.definition: To expect something and often prepare for it before it happens.
cards.example: Planners failed to anticipate the rapid growth in car ownership.
cards.warning: No significa "adelantar" (dinero o una fecha): eso es "advance" / "bring forward".

cards.definition: To tell someone something is true so they do not worry; to make certain.
cards.example: Officials assured residents that the water was safe to drink.
cards.warning: "Assure" lleva persona: "assure SOMEONE that". Para "asegurarse de algo" usa "ensure" o "make sure".

cards.definition: To succeed in achieving something after effort.
cards.example: Fewer than half of the pupils attained the expected standard in mathematics.

cards.definition: Used in 'on behalf of' to mean representing or in the interests of someone.
cards.es: en nombre de, en representación de
cards.example: Unions negotiate on behalf of their members for better pay.
cards.warning: Solo se usa en la expresión "on behalf of" (en EE. UU. también "in behalf of").

cards.definition: The largest part of something; a large quantity.
cards.example: The bulk of household waste ends up in landfill sites.

cards.definition: To stop happening or existing (formal).
cards.example: The factory ceased production in 2015 due to falling demand.

cards.definition: Logical, clear and well organised, so that the parts fit together.
cards.example: A coherent essay links each paragraph clearly to the main argument.
cards.warning: "Coherence and Cohesion" es uno de los cuatro criterios de nota de IELTS Writing.

cards.definition: To happen at the same time; to be the same or very similar.
cards.example: The rise in crime coincided with a sharp increase in unemployment.

cards.definition: To begin (formal).
cards.example: Construction of the new hospital will commence next spring.
cards.warning: En EE. UU., "commencement" es la ceremonia de graduación.

cards.definition: Able to exist or work together without problems.
cards.example: Economic growth need not be incompatible with environmental protection.

cards.definition: Happening or existing at the same time.
cards.example: The two studies were carried out concurrently in different countries.
cards.warning: "Concurrido" (lleno de gente) es "crowded", no "concurrent".

cards.definition: To keep something within limits; to keep someone in a closed space.
cards.example: The problem is not confined to large cities; it also affects rural towns.

cards.definition: Strong public disagreement about something.
cards.example: The use of animals in medical research remains a subject of controversy.

cards.definition: The opposite of a statement or fact; also, to have a conversation (formal).
cards.example: Wealth may improve health, but the converse is also true: poor health reduces income.
cards.warning: "Conversely" (por el contrario) es un conector excelente para contrastar en Writing.

cards.definition: A machine or tool designed for a particular purpose; a method used to produce an effect.
cards.example: Most teenagers spend several hours a day on mobile devices.
cards.warning: "Device" (sustantivo) vs "devise" (verbo: idear, diseñar).

cards.definition: To give time, money or effort to a particular activity or purpose.
cards.example: Governments should devote more resources to preventive healthcare.
cards.warning: "Devote to + -ing": "devote time to studying", no "to study".

cards.definition: To become or make something smaller, weaker or less important.
cards.example: The influence of traditional newspapers has diminished in the digital age.

cards.definition: To change the shape or meaning of something so it is no longer true or accurate.
cards.example: Selective reporting can distort the public's understanding of risk.

cards.definition: The length of time that something lasts.
cards.example: Participants were asked to record the duration of each exercise session.

cards.definition: To gradually damage or destroy something, by natural forces or over time.
cards.example: Repeated scandals have eroded public trust in politicians.

cards.definition: A set of moral principles; the moral rules that control behaviour.
cards.example: Medical ethics require doctors to obtain informed consent from patients.
cards.warning: La disciplina es "ethics" (con -s) y se usa con verbo en singular o plural según el sentido.

cards.definition: The way something is arranged, organised or presented.
cards.example: The new exam format includes shorter, more frequent tasks.

cards.definition: To start an organisation or institution; to base something on an idea.
cards.example: The university was founded in 1850 to train engineers.
cards.warning: "Found" (fundar) es regular: found - founded - founded. No confundir con "found", pasado de "find".

cards.definition: Existing as a natural or permanent part of something.
cards.example: There are risks inherent in any new medical treatment.

cards.definition: A clear, deep understanding of a complex situation or problem.
cards.example: The interviews provide valuable insight into the lives of farm workers.

cards.definition: Necessary and important as part of a whole.
cards.example: Community involvement is integral to the success of conservation projects.
cards.warning: "Integral part" = parte esencial. "Pan integral" es "wholemeal bread".

cards.definition: Between two levels or stages; neither basic nor advanced.
cards.example: An intermediate stage of processing removes impurities from the water.

cards.definition: Done with the hands or by people rather than machines; a book of instructions.
cards.example: Automation has reduced the demand for manual labour in factories.

cards.definition: Fully grown or developed; behaving in a sensible adult way; to become fully developed.
cards.example: Mature students often bring valuable work experience to university courses.
cards.warning: "Mature student" = estudiante adulto (mayor de 21-25 años).

cards.definition: To try to end a disagreement between two groups by talking to both.
cards.example: An independent body was appointed to mediate between the union and management.

cards.definition: A way of communicating or expressing something; of middle size or level.
cards.example: English is the medium of instruction in many international schools.

cards.definition: Relating to the armed forces; the armed forces of a country.
cards.example: Several technologies, including GPS, were originally developed for military use.
cards.warning: "A military" (un militar como persona) no existe: se dice "a soldier" o "an officer".

cards.definition: Very small in amount or degree.
cards.example: The new procedure causes minimal discomfort to patients.

cards.definition: Felt or done by two or more people or groups towards each other; shared.
cards.example: Trade agreements are based on mutual benefit.
cards.warning: "Mutually exclusive" = incompatibles entre sí.

cards.definition: A usual or expected way of behaving; a typical standard or pattern.
cards.example: Working from home has become the norm in many technology companies.
cards.warning: Una "norma" como regla escrita suele ser "rule" o "regulation"; "norm" es lo habitual o socialmente esperado.

cards.definition: To cover part of the same area or share some features with something else.
cards.example: The responsibilities of the two departments overlap considerably.

cards.definition: Accepting what happens without trying to change it; not active.
cards.example: Watching television is a largely passive activity.
cards.warning: La voz pasiva ("It is argued that...") es muy útil en Writing académico.

cards.definition: A part of something larger; an amount of food for one person.
cards.example: A large portion of the budget is spent on staff salaries.
cards.warning: No confundir con "proportion" (proporción).

cards.definition: Coming before a more important action or event; initial and not final.
cards.example: Preliminary results suggest that the vaccine is highly effective.

cards.definition: A set of official rules or procedures; an international agreement.
cards.example: Hospitals must follow strict protocols to prevent the spread of infection.

cards.definition: Relating to quality or characteristics rather than to numbers or quantity.
cards.example: The researchers used qualitative interviews to explore teachers' experiences.
cards.warning: Su opuesto es "quantitative" (cuantitativo).

cards.definition: To improve something by making small changes; to make a substance pure.
cards.example: The model was refined after the first round of testing.

cards.definition: To rest and become calm; to make a rule or control less strict.
cards.example: The government relaxed restrictions on foreign investment.
cards.warning: "Relaxed" = relajado (persona); "relaxing" = relajante (actividad).

cards.definition: To stop someone or something from doing something; to keep under control.
cards.example: Higher interest rates are intended to restrain inflation.
cards.warning: No confundir con "restrict" (restringir) ni con "refrain" (abstenerse).

cards.definition: A complete change in methods or ideas; the violent overthrow of a government.
cards.example: The digital revolution has transformed how people work and communicate.

cards.definition: Stiff and not able to bend; very strict and difficult to change.
cards.example: Rigid rules can discourage teachers from trying new methods.

cards.definition: A way from one place to another; a method of achieving something.
cards.example: Education is seen as the main route out of poverty.

cards.definition: A description of a possible future situation or series of events.
cards.example: In the worst-case scenario, sea levels could rise by over a metre.
cards.warning: Falso amigo: el "escenario" de un teatro es "stage"; "scenario" es una situación hipotética.

cards.definition: An area of activity, influence or interest; a perfectly round 3D shape.
cards.example: Women remain under-represented in the political sphere.

cards.definition: Lower in rank or less important; a person with a lower position at work.
cards.example: Environmental concerns are often treated as subordinate to economic goals.

cards.definition: Something added to improve or complete something; to add to something.
cards.example: Many retired people supplement their pensions with part-time work.

cards.definition: To stop something for a period of time; to hang something.
cards.example: Train services were suspended during the storm.
cards.warning: Falso amigo: "suspender un examen" es "fail an exam", no "suspend".

cards.definition: A group of people who work together or play a sport together.
cards.example: A team of researchers from three universities conducted the study.

cards.definition: Lasting or used for only a limited period of time.
cards.example: Many young people work on temporary contracts with few benefits.
cards.warning: "Trabajo temporal" = "temporary job". En inglés, "temporal" significa "relativo al tiempo" y no equivale a "temporary"; y "un temporal" (tormenta) es "a storm".

cards.definition: To cause something to start happening, often suddenly; the cause of an event.
cards.example: The rise in food prices triggered protests in several cities.

cards.definition: To bring parts together to form a single whole.
cards.example: A common language helped to unify the different regions of the country.

cards.definition: To break a law, agreement or principle; to fail to respect someone's rights.
cards.example: Collecting personal data without consent may violate privacy laws.
cards.warning: En inglés "violate" casi nunca se usa para agresión sexual (eso es "rape"); se usa para leyes y derechos.

cards.definition: The ability to see; an idea or plan of what the future could be like.
cards.example: The mayor set out a vision of a car-free city centre.
